sections.h2: How does property tax work for someone selling in Worth County?
sections.html:
In Worth County the tax commissioner bills and collects, while the Board of Tax Assessors alone decides what a property is worth. The commissioner is an independently elected office, so it does not answer to the assessors or the county commissioners. A seller needs the bill from one office and the value history from the other.

Worth County was carved out of Dooly and Irwin counties in December 1853 and became Georgia's 106th county. Sylvester is both the county seat and the largest city. Parts of Worth were later used to form Tift and Turner counties in 1905. Cotton, peanuts and poultry are the farm products Wikipedia names as the base of the local economy, and Worth is part of the Albany metropolitan area.

The state's rule for sales is simple. If you owned the parcel on January 1, you owe that year's tax, and Georgia does not return any of it because you sold in March or June. Plan the closing statement around that fact.

sections.h2: Which Worth County office should I call?
sections.html:
Call the tax commissioner for bills and payoffs, and call the assessors for values, returns and exemptions.

Payment options on the tax site include paying online, mailing a check to the Room 15 address, calling in a payment, and using the drop box in the alley between the courthouse and the jail.

sections.h2: When is the Worth County property tax bill due?
sections.html:
The county tax site describes two installments for real estate and personal property: the first by October 15 and the second by November 15. Mobile and manufactured homes are due April 1. When a date falls on a weekend, it moves to the next business day.

Those are the dates the tax office publishes in its FAQ. Because billing schedules shift with the digest, read the due date printed on your own bill and confirm it with the office if you are planning a closing near a deadline.

The Georgia Department of Revenue adds a general rule for every county: the official date is December 20 unless the local government moves it, and each taxpayer has 60 days from the postmark of the bill before interest accrues. Penalties can follow on unpaid balances. Ask the commissioner's office for the exact late charges when you request a payoff.

  • The tax office honors only a United States Postal Service date stamp as proof of timely payment. A meter stamp does not count.
  • Partial payments are accepted, though interest and penalties keep running on what remains.
  • Bills go to the owner of record. The office sends a data file to mortgage companies but does not mail them the bill, so forward it yourself if your lender pays through escrow.

sections.h2: What is the solid waste fee on a Worth County tax bill?
sections.html:
Owners in the unincorporated part of the county with a residential or business structure pay an annual solid waste fee of $264.00 that rides on the property tax bill. The Board of Commissioners adopted this by resolution beginning in 2019.

Two relief paths exist. If a structure is dilapidated or vacant for the entire year, the owner can file a waiver request for the Board of Commissioners to approve. Owners over 65 whose total household income is $15,200 or less can qualify for an elderly exemption by completing an affidavit at the commissioners' office, reachable at (229) 776-8200, extension 1.

This matters in a sale because an inherited or empty rural house may carry the fee even when nobody has lived there. Ask whether a waiver was ever filed, and include any unpaid fee in the payoff figure.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Worth County assessment?
sections.html:
Send a written appeal to the Board of Tax Assessors within 45 days of the date on your assessment notice. The appeal may rest on taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption, and it must state which method of appeal you choose.

Each year from January 1 to April 1, owners can file a return declaring the value they believe is right. The assessors review that figure. If they disagree, they mail a notice with their own value, and the 45-day clock starts on that notice. Call (229) 776-8203 for help with the form.

Georgia lists three appeal routes: the county Board of Equalization, a hearing officer, or an arbitrator. The Department of Revenue supervises the system statewide but cannot overrule a local board on a single property. If a refund results from a final value, the state says it must be processed automatically, and separate refund claims for erroneous collection must begin within three years of payment.

sections.h2: How do homestead and other exemptions work in Worth County?
sections.html:
To receive the homestead exemption you must own the house and live in it on January 1. The Tax Assessors' Office approves the applications. You may file at any time of year, yet only an application received before April 1 counts for that year's bill.

Once approved, the exemption continues without a yearly renewal as long as you stay in the same house. A move or a change to the deed means filing again. For a seller, that means a buyer should file in their own name after closing rather than assume the exemption transfers.

Other programs the county tax site mentions:

  • The freeport exemption for business personal property, handled by the assessors.
  • Special assessment programs, which the assessors can describe by phone.
  • The elderly exemption from the solid waste fee described above.

sections.h2: What if taxes are late or a lien is recorded in Worth County?
sections.html:
The office mails a 30-day notice of intent before it files a lien. A lien, called a FiFa, is recorded on the General Execution Docket kept by the Clerk of Superior Court. Tax unpaid more than 90 days after the due date becomes subject to one, and the record is public, so credit bureaus can see it.

Paying the tax along with the fees, penalties and interest cancels the FiFa. The office says it does not sell tax liens over the counter. If levy and advertisement of a tax sale have started, it recommends paying in person instead of by mail.

Mobile and modular homes are treated as personal property in Georgia. Their owners must file a return and obtain a location permit, and the office will not issue the permit until the current year's mobile home tax is paid in full. A seller with a manufactured home on the lot should settle that account before closing.

sections.h2: What do the numbers say about Worth County housing?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau counted 20,784 people in 2020 and estimates 20,059 for July 2025. For 2020 to 2024 it shows a median owner-occupied home value of $104,900, 73.7% owner occupancy, and 7,739 households. Median gross rent was $864 and median household income was $58,694. Builders took out 61 permits in 2025.

The 2020 census found 9,244 housing units, with 11.5% vacant, and 29.6% of residents lived in urban areas. Workers travel an average of 28.4 minutes to their jobs. The county borders Dougherty, Lee, Crisp, Turner, Tift, Colquitt and Mitchell counties.

These figures are a backdrop only. The number that controls your sale is the payoff the tax commissioner gives you, together with the value on your assessment notice.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in Worth County?
faqs.a: Pay the tax commissioner at 201 N. Main St., Room 15 in Sylvester. You can also pay online, by phone at (229) 776-8204, by mail, or in the drop box between the courthouse and the jail.

faqs.q: What are the Worth County tax due dates?
faqs.a: The county tax FAQ lists October 15 and November 15 for real estate and personal property, and April 1 for mobile homes. Check the date on your bill, since the schedule can change.

faqs.q: How long do I have to dispute my Worth County value?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date of the assessment notice. File the written appeal with the Board of Tax Assessors at (229) 776-8203 and name the appeal method you want.

faqs.q: Does the solid waste fee apply to a vacant house?
faqs.a: It can apply, but a structure that is dilapidated or vacant for the whole year may qualify for a waiver approved by the Board of Commissioners. Call (229) 776-8200, extension 1 to ask.

faqs.q: Will a late payment hurt my credit?
faqs.a: It can if a lien is recorded. Tax unpaid more than 90 days past due can lead to a public FiFa, and credit bureaus may read it. The tax office does not report to the bureaus itself.
